g-kokkos.note: pointer to the Kokkos venue card: linger angle

old.name: Kokkos Cafe Bistro
old.teaser: The strip's default proper café — where the residents take their weekday lunch.
old.body: For years locals called it Diani's only real coffee shop; a quarter-century later it is still the habit — espresso, the house 'kokkoccino' flavoured cappuccinos, and a chef-driven bistro card with local, Asian and European lines. NGO staff, hotel managers and long-stayers hold their meetings here. Sunday closes early (16:30) — confirm, the site's copyright is stale. Diani Beach Road, central · +254 721 565 567 · breakfast and weekday lunch

old.name: Diani Bakehouse
old.teaser: German seed loaves, challah and Berliners — the expat history in a bread basket.
old.body: Beside Apero on the central strip: German breads, cinnamon rolls, jam-filled Berliners, cakes to order. The German-bread list is a living trace of the families who built the first hotels. Publishes almost nothing — confirm on @diani_bakehouse before crossing town, and go early for the proper loaf. Diani Beach Road, beside Apero · liveness unproven, honestly

old.name: Skippers Coliving
old.teaser: Starlink + fibre, solar backup, a pizzeria and Thursday live music — the real infrastructure.
old.body: Diani's first purpose-built nomad base (2023): air-conditioned container rooms with desks, a coworking room on load-balanced Starlink and fibre, triple power backup, gym, plunge pool. Everything else on this list is a café that tolerates laptops; this is the machine. Not a drop-in: four-week stays preferred, short stays fill gaps, outside day-use is a low-season favour to ask for politely. Near the airstrip · WhatsApp +254 793 870 199 · Thursday music nights

old.name: Pallet Cafe, Galu
old.teaser: The deaf-staffed café's coworking corner on the sand — beautiful, breezy, signal honest-to-patchy.
old.body: Beach beds, hammocks, no walls, an art corner, and ordering in the sign language printed on the menu. The coworking corner is the loveliest desk on the coast — and the honest work-truth is that glare, salt breeze and patchy 4G come with it. Beautiful. Close the laptop by four and swim. Galu beachfront · reported 09:00–16:00 — confirm on Instagram · Sundays bring live music, not focus

old.name: Asha Boutique Bistro
old.teaser: The one beach-side room with outlets and workable wifi — laptop at lunch, never at dinner.
old.body: The 2022 survey's only beach-side venue with genuinely laptop-friendly seating, enough power and decent wifi (30 down) — palm shade, ocean in view, sand off the keyboard. Friday night flips it into the all-you-can-eat BBQ with live guitar, at which point the laptop rule is absolute. Beachfront, central strip · +254 115 065 158 · wifi data is 2022 — verify

old.name: The 41 Beach Club
old.teaser: A bar around an ancient baobab, bao boards on the counter, jazz on the calendar.
old.body: The Forty Thieves succession, solar-powered: sundowner dhow cruises at KES 5,000, a Koroga corner, live jazz and the strip's most sociable Saturday afternoon. Full card in the Tables. Central strip · WhatsApp +254 758 423 283

old.name: Sails at Almanara
old.teaser: The most graceful one-drink room on Galu — white canvas catching the last light.
old.body: The grand-hotel-bar hour of this coast: a sundowner under the sail canopies, officially open to non-residents, with the option of staying for chef Anthony Huth's dinner. Full-moon nights stage dinner on the moonlit sand. Galu · +254 711 852 026 · golden hour, book the sunset tables

old.name: Salty Squid at kite-o'clock
old.teaser: Chilli-mango margaritas while the instructors land in front of the terrace.
old.body: The kite crowd's sunset: Galu's sky traffic on final approach, garlic prawns, and the sister bar team's cocktails. An early room by design — kitchen closes 20:30, bar 21:30. Galu, next to H2O Extreme · +254 758 515 609

b-funky.group: After dark — the clubs, with asterisks

old.group: The bar that earned the chips
old.name: Funky Monkey
old.teaser: Smoked Negronis in a roadside courtyard — the coast's first bar on 50 Best Discovery.
old.body: Opened July 2022 by the Salty Squid team and promptly ranked: the first bar on the Kenyan coast listed on 50 Best Discovery, and a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards Middle East & Africa Top-10 honoree in both Best International Bar Team and Best International Restaurant Bar three years running — 2024, 2025, 2026. Kenyan ingredients worked into classics; Wednesday is Hot Salsa night with DJs and margarita flights. Kitchen to 21:30; last call midnight Wed–Sat. Roadside courtyard, central strip · WhatsApp +254 742 794 527 · Wednesdays, or any late week night

b-manyatta.group: After dark — the clubs, with asterisks
b-manyatta.note: cut clubs: Full Moon, Tandoori — name them only as 'others listed in 2024, nothing verifiable'

old.name: Manyatta
old.teaser: The most local of the strip's clubs — Kenyan prices, Kenyan playlists.
old.body: Where Ukunda drinks and dances: no polish, no tourist premium, the counterweight to the beach-bar circuit. Weakest paper trail of the four — go with a local driver who knows the door. Central strip · weekends

old.name: Full Moon
old.teaser: The revival's headline club — Afrobeat, amapiano, a rooftop lounge.
old.body: Named first in the Nation/NTV nightlife-revival report; aggregators list nightly hours, karaoke and talent nights; its own Instagram sleeps since 2022. Saturday after midnight is the honest bet. North-central strip · no verifiable phone — check IG day-of

old.name: Tandoori International
old.teaser: The veteran complex — 'Every night counts.'
old.body: Club plus the attached Baharini discothèque, sports screens, mixed local-tourist crowd — one of the four names of the 2024 revival, with no current channel to verify. Weekend, late. Central strip · walk-in, cash

b-shakatak.group: After dark — the clubs, with asterisks

old.name: Shakatak
old.teaser: Thirty-plus years of coast disco, by its own count — nothing happens before midnight.
old.body: Two air-conditioned rooms, a garden bar, a monthly 'Dschungel Party' and a website last touched in March 2023. If it is running — have your driver confirm — expect the old-school, hard-edged coast disco in full, and plan your exit before you need it. Central strip, opposite the hotel row · cash

old.name: The palm-wine dens
old.teaser: Unsigned village living rooms where the tappers' wine is poured hours off the palm.
old.body: Mnazi is drunk in mangwe — unnamed dens in the Ukunda backstreets and the villages, where selling is traditionally a woman's trade. The economy is real: some 2,800 tappers coast-wide, licences re-vetted county-wide in 2024, coast leaders defending the drink publicly as heritage. The one honest visitor door is the Kaaribu tour's tasting stop (USD 25, includes the introduction that matters). Fermentation continues in the bottle; hygiene varies with the den and the hour. Guests go guided or not at all — a mangwe is a neighbourhood's living room, not an attraction. Ukunda backstreets, Kinondo, Msambweni · late afternoon, with a local

o-shimba.note: one home for Shimba and the falls

old.name: Shimba Hills
old.teaser: Kenya's last breeding sable herd, forest elephants, Sheldrick Falls.
old.body: The one-day green counterweight: coastal rainforest, sable on the dawn glades, the ranger-walked falls. Full brief in The sacred forest & the colobus . USD 50 non-resident (KWS 2025 schedule) — the fee that surprises people; budget it. Via Kombani junction · gates 06:00–18:00 · cashless

old.name: Shimba Hills & Sheldrick Falls
old.teaser: Kenya's largest coastal rainforest and its last breeding sable antelope — be there at the gate.
old.body: 192.5 km² first protected in 1903, gazetted 1968: the country's last breeding herd of the critically endangered sable antelope, forest elephants, mist over the glades, ocean views back to the coast, and the ranger-escorted walk down to Sheldrick Falls. In via Kombani junction, 31 km from Diani; gates 06:00–18:00, cashless (KWSpay). The honest brief: forest, not savannah — you come for sable, elephants, mist and the falls, not Mara density. Non-resident fees rose to USD 50 adult in the October 2025 schedule; old blogs still quote KES 300. Kubo/Matuga, inland Kwale · sable graze the glades early — gate at 06:00 or don't bother

old.name: Sheldrick Falls
old.teaser: The waterfall walk inside Shimba Hills — carry water, wear real shoes.
old.body: The signed trailhead inside the reserve sends you down with a ranger to the falls — the green hour of the Shimba day between the sable glades and the viewpoints. Brief in the green section . Shimba Hills · mornings, before the heat climbs the hill

old.name: Funzi & the Ramisi estuary
old.teaser: The quieter island day — crocodiles on the ebb, a sandbank swim, crab on Funzi.
old.body: Boards at Bodo village; briefed in The dhow day 's quieter-waters list. The Funzi Keys resort itself is almost certainly not trading — do not let stale online listings sell you a closed island lodge. 5–10 h day · community fees bundled by operators

old.name: Funzi Island day
old.teaser: Mangrove river, crocodiles on the ebb, a sandbank swim, crab lunch on the island.
old.body: Boards at Bodo village, cruises the Ramisi River estuary looking for crocodiles where river meets ocean, swims off a tidal sandbank and ends with crab, grilled fish and coconut rice on Funzi. No marine park here — community fees are bundled by the operator. Crocodiles are not guaranteed; the sandbank drowns at high water, so timing is everything; ask exactly who cooks the lunch and where. ~35 km south · 5–10 h with hotel pickup ~07:30 · private boats negotiable at Bodo

o-mombasa.group: North — half a day in Mombasa
o-mombasa.note: the route and timing; the street and the co-op have their own cards: point, do not retell

old.name: The Biashara Street & Akamba run
old.teaser: Kangas at the 1887 house, carvings in the sheds they were cut in.
old.body: Pair the kanga street (morning) with the carving co-operative (on the airport side) and you have replaced every curio stall on the strip with the real thing — briefs in Crafts & the hand . Add Mombasa Old Town if the day stretches. Via Dongo Kundu · 45–75 min each way depending on traffic

p-mwaepe.group: The fish — two landings and the names
p-mwaepe.note: pointer-ish: the buying angle; the venue card holds the place

old.name: Mwaepe landing (BMU)
old.teaser: Whole changu, snapper and pweza off the sand — the walkable landing of the Galu hotels.
old.body: One of the seven artisanal stations of the Diani–Chale fishery, and the one you can walk to. The fishermen's Beach Management Unit reclaimed this ground from land-grabbers and holds title; a KSh 256 million upgrade — ice plant, fish banda, boatyard — broke ground in March 2025, because ice has historically been the missing link. Buy on the incoming tide, judge by eye and gill, ice immediately, cook the same day. Some kusi mornings nothing comes in; that is the sea, not a failure. Galu/Kinondo · cash · ask for the BMU chairman if buying quantity · the fishermen's own two shacks cook what you point at

p-shimoni.group: The fish — two landings and the names

old.name: Shimoni landing & the new port
old.teaser: Tuna and kingfish class off the channel — beside Kenya's first purpose-built fish port, not yet open.
old.body: The channel fishery lands bigger fish than Diani's reef. The KSh 2.6 billion KPA port (200 t/day jetty, cold store, 8 t/day ice) was completed and handed over in July 2025 but awaited an operator and commissioning at last dated evidence — so buy at the village landing as ever, and treat the shiny port as 'in transition', not a market. Loin the tuna on the spot; the drive back is an hour-plus of warm truck. Shimoni · pair with the dhow day · privatisation reports ran into March 2026

p-names.group: The fish — two landings and the names

old.name: Changu, pweza, tafi — the name ladder
old.teaser: The fish's name encodes where it was caught, with what gear, and how it ranks — learn ten words.
old.body: Fisher Swahili is a technical language of its own, documented in Heidi Glaesel's coast fieldwork: changu the emperors (tangu at Msambweni), tafi the rabbitfish in graded varieties, pono the parrotfish, tewa the groupers told apart like leopards — tewa chui, the leopard grouper — kolekole the trevallies, nguru the kingfish, jodari the tunas, pweza the octopus, kamba the shrimp and kamba mawe the lobster. The grading lore is a fallen hierarchy in plain sight: tafi, changu and pono dominate today's catch, but were less desired when tuna, marlin and kingfish ran thick a few decades ago — by the late 1990s kolekole and nguru were already marked rarely caught. And one proverb outranks every species name: Chambo chema ni baraka ya mvuvi — good bait is the fisher's blessing. ★ The old hand's point: a tewa chui is a trap-and-line lagoon fish; a sulisuli means someone crossed the reef into big water. Ask for kitoweo-grade fish by its fisher name and you are asking, in one word, for the fish the fisher feeds his own children — the grade never on display. Treat any cheap nguru with suspicion; the old men will tell you exactly why there is so little of it. The morning auctions at Gazi, Mwaepe and Msambweni are living dictionaries — point, ask the name, ask 'ya leo?'

p-market.note: Ibiza Market is cut: say trade is moving here, do not recommend Ibiza

old.name: Diani Modern Market, Mvindeni
old.teaser: The south coast's newest food fact — produce rows with actual cold storage behind them.
old.body: Commissioned 23 May 2026: a Sh50-million covered market replacing the old open-air Ukunda market whose traders spent years in rain, dust and theft. Cold storage, a forming food court, an ICT hub, a mothers' room — and already tight on market days, which is the best review a market can get. The cooked-food court is still settling; the produce rows are the point. Mvindeni, Ukunda–Ramisi road side · mornings · cash/M-Pesa

old.group: The coconut ladder — one tree, one economy
old.name: Madafu · mnazi · mbata · makuti
old.teaser: Drinking nut, palm wine, copra, thatch — most coastal farm households live off this one tree.
old.body: Madafu is the green drinking nut, opened roadside. Mnazi is the tapped palm wine — a morning product, drunk the same day. Mbata is the mature copra, graded milling (for oil) versus edible (chewed dry); the kitchens grate it on the mbuzi stool and press the cream by hand. Makuti thatch and coir rope use the rest. Chef's rule: madafu for guests, Kentaste for the pantry, mnazi only where it is tapped, before noon, where locals queue — and never serve it to guests untested. Everywhere in Kwale · the fruit calendar peaks with mangoes Nov–Mar (Ngowe Dec–Jan)

p-carrefour.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs

old.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs
old.name: Carrefour, Centre Point
old.teaser: Fish counter, butchery, bakery — the strip's serious one-stop, Kentaste on the shelf.
old.body: Kwale's first Carrefour solves what the open market cannot: the cold chain. Dairy, dry stores, back-up protein, and the locally pressed coconut line at source prices. Honest limits: imported specialty depth — cheese, charcuterie, wine — stays thinner than Nairobi. Plan around it or brief the provisioner. Centre Point Plaza, Ukunda junction · ~08:30–21:00 typical, unverified first-party

p-chandarana.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs

old.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs
old.name: Chandarana Foodplus
old.teaser: Masalas, ghee, atta, dry mbaazi — the pantry for the coast's actual cooking.
old.body: The Kenyan family chain's south-coast outpost, strong on specialty, imported and Indian-Kenyan lines, wines and spirits. When the brief calls for cardamom, ghee or atta rather than French butter, this is the aisle — and the dry pigeon peas for a proper mbaazi live here too. Baharini Plaza, central strip · ~08:00–21:00 (directory-sourced) · +254 712 354 955

p-naivas.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs

old.group: The cold chain — three supermarkets, three jobs
old.name: Naivas, The Gate Mall
old.teaser: Kenya's biggest homegrown chain — bulk staples where the locals shop.
old.body: A step cheaper than the beach-road pair, inland at the Gate Mall: dry staples, crates of water, cleaning, the unglamorous volume. Do bulk here, the cold chain on the strip, and the living produce at the market — three stops, three jobs. Aggregator hours conflict; call before an early run. Ukunda–Ramisi road · with the market in the same run

f-early.group: The gap, and how to plan around it

old.group: The gap, and how to plan around it
old.name: Kitchens close earlier than you think
old.teaser: The Salty Squid's kitchen shuts at half eight. Always.
old.body: Several beach kitchens here stop serving well before the evening feels finished — The Salty Squid 's closes at 20:30 without exception, and it is not the only one. If you are coming off a late dive, a sunset dhow or a long drive back from Shimoni, order by eight or accept that you are eating at a junction later. Eat early, or eat inland — those are the two options after nine on the beach road

f-midnight.group: The gap, and how to plan around it
f-midnight.note: name only the kept clubs: Shakatak, Manyatta

old.group: The gap, and how to plan around it
old.name: Nothing moves before midnight
old.teaser: The night here starts after the food has stopped, not with it.
old.body: Diani's clubs — Shakatak , Full Moon , Tandoori , Manyatta — are empty before midnight and then everything at once. Shakatak's own description is exactly that. So the sequence that works is: eat properly by nine, drink somewhere on the sand until eleven, and go out after that. Trying to do it in the other order leaves you hungry. ⚠ Confirm any club on its own channel the same day. Several have a 2024 press trail from the streetlight-driven nightlife revival and a web presence that then goes cold — that gap is the caveat, not a detail. Weekend nights · cash and walk-in at most of them

old.name: The Ukunda junction, just after sunset
old.teaser: Where the boda riders and shop staff who run the strip eat — and it is cheap.
old.body: From late afternoon the junction fills with charcoal and karai pans: viazi karai in turmeric batter with chilli-tamarind, mishkaki over the coals, grilled corn at about twenty shillings. It sits at the town's transport heart, which is why it is still going when the beach road has gone quiet, and why the people eating there are the people who work here. KES 20 corn to low hundreds (obs. 2026-05) · walk up, point, pay cash or M-Pesa

old.name: Havana's late kitchen
old.teaser: The one strip address that will still feed you when the others have stopped.
old.body: Havana is the late plate on the beach road itself — the reason it appears on the Tuesday and Saturday lines of the week . If you are staying on the strip and do not want a taxi to a junction, this is the answer. Check the night before you rely on it; late service is the first thing to go in low season

old.name: Funky Monkey, to midnight
old.teaser: Bar food while the strip's one institutional party night runs.
old.body: The bar runs to midnight Wednesday to Saturday , with the Hot Salsa night on Wednesdays — DJs, dancers, margarita flights. It bridges the gap between the kitchens closing and the clubs opening, which on this strip is a genuine service. WhatsApp a table for the Wednesday salsa night
